svg.text: How fetchers work
A fetcher retrieves the bytes behind a URL and nothing else.
Consumer-owned, one module per transport or host -- never per format.
committed to your repo
engine-side
answer time (the refer plane)
refusal / skipped
1 - WHICH FETCHER RETRIEVES THIS URL (resolved once, at fux add)
The URL line: fetch=<stem> decoder=<stem>
https://x.sharepoint.com/hr/p.xlsx
fetch=cdp decoder=xlsx keep=true ttl=24h
BOTH MANDATORY, never empty (W-199 D1, DoD 10).
Written once by fux add; a line missing either
fails to parse. Every line is a pin: a route
changed later does not move it.
fux doctor's pinned-fetchers row reports the drift;
--fetch / --decoder pin either by hand, offline.
fux.toml [sources.url.routes]
"*.sharepoint.com" = "cdp"
"wiki.acme.in:8443" = "http"
"re:^docs-\d+\.acme\.in$" = "own"
Key is the HOST: host, *.host, host:port,
or a re: pattern. Literals rank host:port >
host > *.host; *.host never matches the apex.
A regex never competes: two matches = HARD ERROR.
fux doctor's fetcher-routes row checks the table.
ROUTES claim in the module
.fux/fetchers/own.py:
ROUTES = {"*.atlassian.net": "own"}
Drop a file in and it works. Read from
source with ast, NEVER imported --
doctor stays offline and a consumer's
missing dependency cannot break resolve.
The shipped http.py / cdp.py claim nothing: a
shipped claim would be fux's opinion about your hosts.
wins
wins
THERE IS NO DEFAULT LAYER (W-199 D2).
--fetch not given, no route, no claim -> fux add REFUSES, naming the hosts it tried and the fetcher stems on disk.
[sources.url] fetcher is gone and the directory is fixed at .fux/fetchers/. Nothing escalates from http to cdp -- a human writes fetch=cdp on the line.
2 - THE PROTOCOL A FETCHER IMPLEMENTS
ROUTES = {"*.atlassian.net": "own"}
# optional claim; read with ast
MAX_PARALLEL = 1
# optional; absent means 1
def fetch(url: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]
# REQUIRED: (bytes, Content-Type)
def configure(config: dict) -> None
# [sources.url.config], yours
def connect() -> None / def close() -> None
# once per batch; close on raise
def validate(url: str) -> str | None
# ETag / Last-Modified token
def is_rate_limited(exc) -> bool
# declared, never sniffed
Retrieval only. A fetcher that returned Markdown made the index depend on WHICH fetcher
ran (W-86 P8). Fux never sees a status code: the fetcher speaks HTTP (or CDP); fux does not.
What the return value means
(bytes, type) -> refusal rules, then the LINE's decoder
a str anywhere -> this URL is SKIPPED by name (W-253)
fetch() raises -> SKIPPED; run continues, prior record kept
rate-limited -> 3 retries, doubling backoff, host counted
validate() same -> body fetch skipped; sha still compared
A str return was read as prose until 3.0; now BREAKING.
The fix is return body.encode(), content_type.
MAX_PARALLEL is capability; [sources.url] max_parallel is policy
and can only lower it. Retry-After is never read.
3 - WHERE A FETCHER SITS IN INGEST (one URL line, left to right)
URL line
fetch=cdp decoder=xlsx
.fux/fetchers/cdp.py
fetch(url)
(bytes, type)
refusal check: a sign-in page?
acquired blob
.fux/acquired/ (keep=true)
.fux/decoders/xlsx.py
the line's decoder= *
Markdown
extract, PII, index
refused: a skipped row, nothing retained
1. the magic floor, always on, vs the LINE's decoder
2. .fux/refusals.toml rules, file order, first match wins
missing file = no rules; malformed = the run stops before
the first socket opens. Rule hit counts reach fux doctor.
* decoder= is the ONLY thing consulted (DoD 10, shipped 2026-09-21).
The Content-Type is observed ONCE, by fux add, to propose the stem;
ingest never reads the header. The blob's extension comes from the
decoder too, so .fux/acquired/ names files by what they are.
.fux/index/REGISTER (W-199 D4) -- committed beside the index it describes
loc . kind . sha . decoder . fetcher
one sorted line per indexed document; no clock, no run id (L4); paths and hashes, never content (L3).
The ruled fifth column, outcome, is a fact about a run -- kind (file / url) replaced it (SR-INGEST d22).
4 - THE SAME PAIR AT ANSWER TIME (the refer plane)
fux answer cites a URL -> the SAME pinned fetcher re-fetches it, the SAME declared decoder re-decodes it, a fresh sha is compared.
Fetchers are loaded per URL from the line's fetch= (one connect per module); the decoder is declared_decoder(), read off the same committed line ingest read.
Verdicts: current . stale . cached (within ttl=) . as-ingested (source unreachable; the retained bytes in .fux/acquired/ still match) . unverified.
[sources.url] fetch_at_answer = false opens no socket at answer time and answers from .fux/acquired/. This is why the pair lives on the line, not in a fetcher.
THE TWO ASYMMETRIES THAT MATTER
A fetcher is keyed on WHERE (transport, host); a decoder on WHAT (format).
One cdp fetcher serves .xlsx, .html and .pdf alike; the line pairs them. There is no "xlsx fetcher".
A link found inside a decoded page is an EDGE, never a fetch.
edges.py: a ref edge if its target is already in the index; otherwise nothing. The corpus is the list.
Following links at ingest would make the index depend on a crawl frontier (L4), reach beyond the fenced list (L5) and index pages nobody declared (L3).
cdp.py ships extract_links() and nothing in fux calls it: a crawl, if you want one, is the fetcher's to write, because the decoder plane may not open a socket.
Drawn from the code, 2026-10-05. src/fux/ingest/urlsrc.py, routes.py, register.py, refusals.py, edges.py, src/fux/templates/http.py.txt, cdp.py.txt, refusals.toml.txt,
src/fux/refer/source.py, src/fux/query/refer_answer.py. SR-FETCHER (0117) - SR-HTTP-FETCHER (0119) - SR-CDP-FETCHER (0118) - SR-URL-LIST (0116) - SR-CONFIG (0113) - SR-REFUSAL (0146) -
SR-ACQUIRED (0145) - SR-URL-FRESHNESS (0147) - SR-REFER-PLANE (0127). Decoders: architecture-decoders.svg. The model-vs-built comparison: architecture-fetchers-compare.svg.
